about: How the Stage cuts a part into levels; CHARTING.md explains every knob. Each part has a ladder of tiers, easiest first, and every tier is the one below plus more (a tier may only loosen a rule). Beginner, Easy, Medium and Hard each name a tier, and Adaptive walks the ladder one step at a time. A tier: notes = chord notes kept, in `keep` order (null = all); hits = the heaviest weight played as written (1 the hits a part stands on, 2 the groove, 3 pushes and ornaments); gap = seconds at least between two onsets; space = seconds at most without an onset (a longer silence borrows a lighter hit; null = never); bonus = points per hit times this. A ladder's phrase (bars) keeps every key the part plays in each phrase at every tier, before the weights; a tier may name a longer phrase of its own (Beginner: four bars). The bottom tier with fromAbove is cut from the chart the tier above makes on its own, so it changes nothing above it. Adaptive: `ahead` bars before each block, the last `window` bars (reaching back to twice that for `judged` notes) decide a drop and the bars played at the current tier (a whole window of them at least, up to two) decide a climb; at or over `climb` it climbs (not while the hits scatter past spreadMaxMs, median ms), under `ease` or after `missRun` misses in a row it drops; then climbs hold for afterClimb / afterDrop blocks (drops never wait); a climb or a drop lands on the next tier whose chart differs; it never sinks under floorBelowStart tiers below where the run began; a run starts `resume` tiers under the top of your last adaptive run of the song and part (`start` the first time); a wrong key counts as a miss in its window.
